# `silk/tls/server_protocol`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Serve TLS 1.3 on a `silk.net.tcp_server` engine, with the certificate chain and private key
loaded from PEM text.

## When to use
Use [`TlsProtocol`](#TlsProtocol) to run any `silk.net.tcp_server` protocol over TLS, as the HTTPS mode of
`silk.http.serve` does. Load the certificate chain and the private key one time with
[`TlsServerConfig.fromPem`](#TlsServerConfig.impl.fromPem), and share the config across all connections and workers.

## Details
Each connection runs one `silk.tls.server` [`Server`](./tls-server.md#Server): the handshake, the record layer,
KeyUpdate and `close_notify` all come from it. The protocol decrypts the bytes that arrive and
gives them to the inner protocol, and encrypts what the inner protocol writes. When the inner
protocol closes the connection, it sends `close_notify` first. The server offers ALPN
`http/1.1` without requiring it.

The private key is an ECDSA P-256 or P-384 key, in a `PRIVATE KEY` (PKCS #8) or
`EC PRIVATE KEY` (SEC 1) block.

## Errors
- [`TlsConfigError`](#TlsConfigError) from [`TlsServerConfig.fromPem`](#TlsServerConfig.impl.fromPem) for PEM text that it cannot use.
- A TLS error on a connection closes that connection without an alert.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if a buffer cannot grow.

## Gotchas
The server does not check its own chain. Give the leaf certificate first. Secrets are not
erased.

Import as `TlsProtocol` with `import silk.tls.server_protocol { TlsProtocol }`.

<a id="TlsConfigError.UnsupportedKey"></a>

The key text holds no `PRIVATE KEY` or `EC PRIVATE KEY` block with a P-256 or P-384 key.

### `KeyMismatch`

<a id="TlsServerConfig"></a>

## `TlsServerConfig`

```silk
pub struct TlsServerConfig
```

The certificate chain and the private key of a server. One config serves every connection and
every worker.

<a id="TlsServerConfig.impl"></a>

## Implementation `TlsServerConfig`

```silk
impl TlsServerConfig
```

<a id="TlsServerConfig.impl.fromPem"></a>

### Associated function `fromPem`

```silk
pub effect fn fromPem(certificates: &[u8], privateKey: &[u8]) -> TlsServerConfig
  ! TlsConfigError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads the certificate chain from the `CERTIFICATE` blocks of `certificates`, leaf first, and
the private key from the first `PRIVATE KEY` (PKCS #8) or `EC PRIVATE KEY` (SEC 1) block of
`privateKey`.

#### Details
It makes one `silk.tls.server` [`Server`](./tls-server.md#Server) to check the chain and the key, so a config that
loads serves every connection.

#### Errors
- `NoCertificate`, `InvalidPem`, `UnsupportedKey`, `ChainTooLarge`, `InvalidCertificate` or
  `KeyMismatch` for input it cannot use.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the chain cannot be stored.

<a id="TlsProtocol"></a>

## `TlsProtocol`

```silk
pub struct TlsProtocol<P>
```

A `silk.net.tcp_server` protocol that serves TLS 1.3 and runs `inner` over the decrypted bytes.

### Details
For each connection it makes a `silk.tls.server` [`Server`](./tls-server.md#Server) and the state of `inner`. Bytes that
arrive are decrypted and given to `inner`, and what `inner` writes is encrypted. When `inner`
closes the connection, the server sends `close_notify` first.
